Careggi — Florence, Italy

Relatively safer day Relatively safer night

In detail

Careggi is dominated by Florence's large university hospital campus and surrounding residential streets. Genuine, repeated press coverage exists of violent assaults against medical staff and security guards inside the Careggi hospital emergency department (multiple incidents with injuries reported in 2024-2025), but this is an internal hospital-violence problem rather than evidence of general street danger to residents or visitors in the surrounding neighbourhood, so the area itself defaults to green. Sources checked: La Nazione / Corriere Toscano, repeated reports of assaults on Careggi hospital staff and security.

Frequently asked questions

Is Careggi safe?

Wandroz currently rates Careggi in Florence as relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Florence during the day and relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Florence at night. This comes from a structured local-source assessment: an area-level review of credible local sources — local and national news, municipal and police-published material, and official surveys where they exist — consolidated across sources rather than taken from a single report. Florence publishes no comparable neighbourhood-level crime dataset; where a city does, Wandroz uses it instead.

Is Careggi safe at night?

At night, Careggi is rated as relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Florence. If you're unsure, it's worth checking recent local reviews for your specific street or block, since a neighbourhood-wide rating can't capture block-by-block variation.

Is Careggi a good area to stay in as a tourist?

Careggi's day rating (relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Florence) is the more relevant one for typical daytime tourist activity; check the night rating too if you'll be out late. Is there official crime data for Careggi?

Not an official government crime feed — Careggi's rating comes from Wandroz's own current local/national press and survey research for this specific area instead (see the note on this page for what was checked and the sources used). An absence of recent negative coverage is treated as inconclusive, not as proof the area is safe. If you live in or know Careggi well, you can suggest a correction using the link below.
